History of the records of one key

Source: R/landmark_journal.R
landmark_journal_history.Rd

Every press of Save is kept in the journals, so the successive passes over one specimen (digitization, then corrections) can be listed and compared – to check that a correction was taken into account, or to see who changed what and when.

Usage

landmark_journal_history(journal_dir, row_key = NULL)

Arguments

journal_dir

Journal directory, or a journal already read with landmark_journal_read().

row_key

Key(s) to inspect (the saved identifier; the species for the FISHMORPH reference target). NULL (default) summarises every key.

Value

A data.frame, one row per record, ordered by key then time: record_id, timestamp, operator, mode, row_key, specimen, species, photo_file, n_points and the per-status counts (n_clicked, n_seeded, n_predicted, n_validated, n_adjusted, n_na).

See also

landmark_journal_status(), consolidate_landmarks() with history = TRUE for the coordinates of every pass.

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "journal_history_demo")
jr <- landmark_journal_open(d, operator = "AT")
#> Session journal: /tmp/Rtmp5ODxC1/journal_history_demo/landmarks_AT_20261027T211330Z.tsv
landmark_journal_append(jr, "fish_01", cbind(c(10, 60), c(20, 22)), 1:2)
landmark_journal_append(jr, "fish_01", cbind(c(11, 60), c(20, 23)), 1:2)
landmark_journal_history(d, "fish_01")
#>                   record_id                timestamp operator mode row_key
#> 1 AT_20261027T211330Z-00001 2026-10-27T21:13:30.919Z       AT      fish_01
#> 2 AT_20261027T211330Z-00002 2026-10-27T21:13:30.921Z       AT      fish_01
#>   specimen species photo_file n_points n_clicked n_seeded n_predicted
#> 1                                    2         2        0           0
#> 2                                    2         2        0           0
#>   n_validated n_adjusted n_na
#> 1           0          0    0
#> 2           0          0    0
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
